hero.title: Open digital public infrastructure
hero.lead: Verifiable data primitives anyone can build on. Sovereign, interoperable, privacy-preserving. Deploy it yourself, fork it, or extend it.
hero.layer1.label: Institutional
hero.layer2.label: Mesh
hero.layer3.label: Ledger
what.label: What
what.title: Infrastructure, not a product
what.desc: Attestto Open assembles open standards into deployable infrastructure for verifiable digital systems. Open schemas, decentralized identifiers, and cryptographic verification that any government, institution, or developer can adopt and extend — with no single-vendor lock-in.
what.card1.title: Open schemas
what.card1.desc: Machine-readable data models that define how verifiable information is structured. Domain-agnostic, extensible by design.
what.card2.title: Decentralized trust
what.card2.desc: Trust comes from transparency and accountability — open code, public proofs, blockchain anchoring — not from taking anyone's word for it. Institutions and private companies alike can serve as trust anchors.
what.card3.title: Privacy at every layer
what.card3.desc: Selective disclosure, zero-knowledge proofs, and minimal data exposure — integrated at the architectural level, not just the protocol layer, so the privacy guarantees hold end-to-end.
arch.title: Three-layer verification
arch.desc: Every piece of verifiable data can be checked at three independent layers. Any two of three is sufficient for full verification.
arch.note: The system degrades gracefully, never catastrophically.
arch.layer1.name: Institutional
arch.layer1.desc: Issuer resolves via DID document hosted at their domain
arch.layer2.name: Mesh
arch.layer2.desc: State synced across a P2P mesh — no central server required
arch.layer3.name: Ledger
arch.layer3.desc: Cryptographic proof anchored on a public, immutable ledger
mesh.title: Distributed mesh network
mesh.desc: Every installation is a node. Citizens, lawyers, and institutions contribute storage to a peer-to-peer mesh that replicates encrypted identity state across the network. No central server. No cloud dependency.
mesh.note: Privacy is not a policy — it is a mathematical guarantee.
mesh.l1.name: Local cache
mesh.l2.name: Mesh peers
mesh.l3.name: Solana anchor
mesh.footprint: ~120 KB per citizen. A national mesh for 5 million people fits in 600 GB distributed across thousands of nodes. Each node stores encrypted data it cannot read — the Blind Courier principle.
principles.label: Principles
principles.title: What we stand for
principles.desc: These principles are non-negotiable. Every component we build, every standard we propose, and every governance decision we make is measured against them.
principles.sovereignty.title: Sovereignty
principles.sovereignty.desc: You control your own data and infrastructure. No external dependency required to operate.
principles.interop.title: Interoperability
principles.interop.desc: Built on W3C, IETF, and ISO standards. If your system is compliant, it works with ours — and vice versa.
principles.privacy.title: Privacy by design
principles.privacy.desc: Data minimization at every layer. Verifiers learn only what they need. Consent is cryptographically enforced, not policy-based.
principles.vendor.title: No vendor lock-in
principles.vendor.desc: Every component is open source, every format is open standard. You can fork it, replace it, or run it yourself. Forever.
principles.reversibility.title: Reversibility
principles.reversibility.desc: Any deployment can export its data in open formats and migrate to another implementation. No trapped data, ever.
principles.transparency.title: Transparency
principles.transparency.desc: Governance decisions, technical choices, and roadmap priorities are public. You can see exactly how and why things change.
principles.neutrality.title: Technological neutrality
principles.neutrality.desc: Blockchain, PKI, cloud, on-premise — the architecture supports all. You pick the stack, not us.
principles.public.title: Public infrastructure
principles.public.desc: The open layer is infrastructure for everyone. Attestto builds products on top — but the foundation is free to use and extend.
source.label: Open Source
source.title: Open source, open standards
source.desc: Reference implementations, schemas, and SDKs. Everything is on GitHub. Fork it, audit it, extend it.
source.did-sns.desc: DID method specification for Solana Name Service domains.
source.vlei.desc: On-chain vLEI attestation with Groth16 zero-knowledge proofs.
source.infra.title: Infrastructure
source.infra.desc: The distributed mesh network and desktop application that turn open standards into running infrastructure.
source.mesh.desc: P2P data mesh over libp2p — encrypted state-sync for sovereign identity.
source.desktop.desc: Electron app — every installation is a mesh node with offline verification.
source.verify.desc: Document verification web components — drop a PDF, verify the math.
source.cr.title: Costa Rica SSI Ecosystem
source.cr.desc: Open schemas and SDKs for Costa Rica's verifiable credential ecosystem — driving licenses, medical certificates, vehicle registrations, and more. Aligned with W3C VDL and ISO 18013-5.
source.cr-schemas.desc: JSON-LD schemas for 11 Costa Rica credential types. W3C VDL + ISO 18013-5.
source.cr-sdk.desc: Typed SDK for issuing and verifying Costa Rica credentials.

governance.label: Governance
governance.title: Stewardship, not control
governance.desc: Attestto Open is stewarded, not owned. The governance model is designed so that no single entity — including Attestto — can unilaterally control the infrastructure, the standards, or the roadmap.
governance.open.title: Open governance
governance.open.desc: Technical decisions are made transparently. Proposals and discussions are public. As the community grows, so does shared decision-making.
governance.contributor.title: Contributor model
governance.contributor.desc: Institutions, governments, and developers can propose schemas, DID methods, and protocol extensions through a structured contribution process.
governance.owner.title: No single owner
governance.owner.desc: The infrastructure is designed to outlive any single organization. Forkable, portable, and built for community governance from day one.
why.title: Your identity. Your proof.
why.lead: Why we built open infrastructure for sovereign identity �� and why it matters that no one owns it.
why.s1_title: Identity is something someone else confirms
why.s1_p1: In most of the world, proving who you are means carrying a physical card, presenting it to an institution, hoping they believe it, and trusting that whoever holds your data won't misuse it.
why.s1_p2: Your identity exists only when someone else says it does. A government office. A bank. A platform. If they lose your record, revoke your access, or simply close for the day — you stop being provable.
why.s1_p3: This isn't a technology problem. It's a design choice. And it can be redesigned.
why.s2_title: When identity depends on someone else
why.s2_p3: These aren't hypothetical. They're happening now, in the countries where we live and build.
why.s3_title: Identity doesn't have to be a favor
why.s3_p1: Identity can be a mathematical proof you carry yourself. W3C Decentralized Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials make this technically possible. A cryptographic key pair on your device. A credential signed by an authority you choose to trust. A proof you present without revealing more than you must.
why.s3_p2: The technology exists. What didn't exist — until now — was open infrastructure to make it deployable. Not a product. Not a platform. Public infrastructure, like roads or the postal service. Anyone can use it, anyone can verify it, anyone can fork it.
why.s4_p1: Existing authorities (governments, professional bodies, universities) issue verifiable credentials signed with their own keys. We don't replace them. We give them a standards-based channel to issue digitally what they already issue on paper.
why.s4_p2: A peer-to-peer network where every node can verify credentials independently, offline, without calling a central server. The credential holder controls what they share and with whom.
why.s4_p3: Cryptographic timestamps on a public ledger prove that a credential existed at a specific time. Not the content — just the proof that it was issued. Immutable, auditable, independent of Attestto.
why.s4_p4: Every component is open source (Apache 2.0). Every standard is W3C or IETF. Any government can fork the entire stack and never depend on us. That's the point.
why.s5_p1: Infrastructure earns trust by what it refuses to do, not by what it promises. These aren't marketing principles. They're constraints we enforce in code.
